column5: 'No fee, no risk, no hassle' — Ampli Energy launch
column6: Renewable energy is now accessible to every SA business, even SMEs and NGOs — no contracts, no capex, just monthly cashback. We are democratising green energy.
column7: SMEs, NGOs, mid-corporates, anyone excluded from traditional long-term PPAs
column8: HIGH — CEO of Discovery + Sasol CEO + Energy Minister at launch. National press coverage. Daily Maverick, Engineering News, BusinessTech.
column9: Strong — differentiated, disruptive, emotionally resonant. First-mover messaging on cashback model.
column10: High — directly threatens Apollo's potential mid-market customers. Month-to-month product vs Apollo's PPA-only positioning.
column11: Act now — Apollo needs a response for the mid-market. What is our answer to a customer who asks 'why should I sign a PPA when Ampli needs nothing from me?'
column14: Electricity Minister Ramokgopa attended. Called it 'democratising' green electrons. Discovery CEO Adrian Gore + Sasol CEO Simon Baloyi fronted it. First tranche already fully subscribed at launch. Customers: Nando's, Vida e Caffè, Hatfield Motors, NetFlorist, NGOs.

column7: Policy makers, investors, media, large C&I buyers
column8: HIGH — independent research gives credibility. Covered in multiple publications.
column9: Strong — smart move to pair product launch with independent research. Positions Discovery Green as market educator.
column10: High — sets the narrative for the mid-market opportunity. Apollo has no equivalent thought leadership piece.
column11: Act — Commission or co-author an independent market insight paper. Apollo needs a thought leadership platform beyond deal announcements.
column14: Research by Krutham (same firm SAETA commissioned). Classic content marketing: fund independent research that validates your product's market rationale.

column14: NOA CEO quote: 'With an estimated 16GW of renewable energy initiatives underway in South Africa's mining sector, the focus is increasingly on execution rather than intent.' Strong, confident positioning.

column14: Andrew Taylor is NOA co-founder and head of trading. Regular op-ed contributor. Apollo needs named spokespeople who are regulars in trade and business media.

column9: Strong — smart diversification messaging. Healthcare angle (Netcare) is unexpected and differentiating.
column10: High — NOA is building a multi-sector narrative before Apollo has established one. Netcare deal signals healthcare sector entry.
column11: Act — Apollo should identify 1-2 unexpected sectors (e.g. agriculture, healthcare, logistics) and make a targeted move. Being first in a sector creates a narrative anchor.
column14: NOA Netcare deal is notable — no other trader has publicly entered healthcare. Smart positioning to show versatility beyond mining.

column14: Enpower CEO James Beatty quote: 'Enpower Trading's approach to the five-year PPA model delivers further liquidity to the market by ensuring financial feasibility for developers for a much wider range of projects.' Smart — addresses both IPP and offtaker concerns simultaneously.

column1: WHAT TO TRACK IN MARKETING & COMMS — Monthly monitoring guide

column4: New campaigns, deal announcements, sector targeting language shifts, executive personal posts, video content, polls, event promotions. The NUMBER of posts is itself a signal — a sudden increase means something is happening.

Visit each competitor's LinkedIn page > Posts > filter 'last 30 days'. Also search the CEO/MD personal profiles of Evan Rice (Etana), Karel Cornelissen (NOA), James Beatty (Enpower), Wayne Cowie (EXSA), Andre Nepgen (Discovery Green), Thembani Bukula (PowerX).

A competitor suddenly posts 3x more than usual = major announcement coming. A new sector hashtag appears (#agri #datacentre #healthcare) = new sector push. A job posting for 'Head of Content' = comms team scaling up.

column1: Key events to monitor for SA electricity traders
column4: Mining Indaba (Feb, Cape Town) — NOA's home ground. African Utility Week (May, Cape Town) — most relevant for traders. C&I Energy+Storage Summit (Nov, Joburg). SANEA events. Nedbank Capital Green Economy Summit. Africa Energy Indaba (Mar, Cape Town).

Which competitor CEOs are speaking? Which panels are traders on? Who is sponsoring? Who is exhibiting? A speaking slot = a message they want to amplify. A sponsorship = a significant budget commitment. No presence at a major event = a gap Apollo can fill.
Apollo currently has NO visible conference presence in research. NOA is dominant at Mining Indaba. Apollo should target African Utility Week 2026 (May) for a speaking slot application immediately.

Energy sector awards: ESI-Africa Energy Awards, Engineering News Awards, Financial Mail Top Empowerment, BUSA Awards, Greentech Capital Innovation Award. Award entries signal what a company wants to be known for — the category they enter is a strategic messaging choice.

When a competitor wins an award, Apollo should enter the same or adjacent category the next cycle. Do not congratulate competitors publicly. Note it here and use it as a trigger to submit Apollo's own entry.

No competitor awards found in recent research — this is a comms opportunity for Apollo. Being first to win a credible energy sector award in the 'pure-play trader' category creates lasting brand equity.

column1: MESSAGING DRIFT (quarterly — compare to Profiles sheet)

column4: When a competitor changes their tag line, value proposition, or key messages, it signals a strategic repositioning. Sometimes subtle — a new word choice like 'firm power' or 'bankable off-take' signals they are targeting a new audience.

Each quarter, visit each competitor's website homepage and note their current tag line and hero message. Compare to what is in the Profiles sheet. If it has changed, update the Profile and note it here as a messaging shift.

Messaging shifts can reveal: entry into a new sector, response to a competitive threat, repositioning away from a struggling market, or anticipation of a regulatory change. The shift from 'renewable energy trader' to 'electricity aggregator' by some players in 2025 was an early signal of the SAWEM market approach.

column1: WHAT APOLLO SHOULD DO — Comms priorities for Q2 2026

column4: Apollo needs a named public voice. MD Jenna Harris or CEO Ed Cameron should be submitting at least 1 op-ed per quarter to Business Day or Engineering News. Topic: 'Why pure-play independent trading is better for SA's energy market.' Frame Reunert backing as credibility without conflict of interest.

Every signed PPA should have a press release. Etana and NOA do this consistently — it builds deal cadence perception and attracts more IPPs and customers. Apollo should aim for at least 1 deal PR per quarter minimum.

Apollo's LinkedIn presence needs to be active. Minimum 2 posts per week: 1 market education post (how trading works, what wheeling is, why IPP-linked vs pure-play matters), 1 company/people post (culture, team, milestones). Do NOT just repost industry news.
